Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking time today. As promised, attaching the rough topology we used in the internal readout (pvpc-controlplane-diagram-v1). We're starting the formal architecture review for our private VPC deployment and want to lock the control-plane/data-plane demarc and the operating checklist before we hit procurement.

Top-level asks from our side:
- Clear list of control-plane outbound dependencies (FQDNs/IPs, ports) and which flows require egress to Redwood managed endpoints vs customer self-hosted control-plane connectors.
- Audit/logging plan: where do API request logs and control-plane audit trails land? Is there a native push to our SIEM or do we pull from a customer-managed S3?
- Secrets & key management: KMS/HSM integration options, rotation cadence, and whether private deployments can use our AWS KMS.
- Egress/MTU/BGP expectations for on-prem edge attachments — we need the expected MTU and BGP community tagging guidance for our colo team.

We'd also like a quick checklist for operational cutover (smoke tests, traffic-shaping rules, fallback model variants) and a list of evidence items for our security team (SOC-like items): control-plane access matrix, TLS certs, signed attestation for data-in-transit protections.

I've cc'd our infra alias — Priya from EdgeWorks may join the hands-on workshop next week.

Thanks,

Marissa / team — quick technical readout and tentative asks: 

1) Control-plane egress list (summary):
- Control API: api.control.redwood-inference.internal (443) — supports TLS mutual auth for private deployments; customer network must allow outbound 443 to a small set of egress IPs (we'll provide CIDR block).
- Metrics/tracing: metrics.ingest.redwood-inference.internal (2200/tcp) or syslog-forward to S3. We can support both push and pull; push uses a short-lived TLS client cert we provision.
- Heartbeat/health checks: /health endpoints over 443; expect occasional 64KB UDP/TCP pings for specific edge relays.

2) Control/data demarcation notes:
- Control-plane traffic is strictly management: model versioning, rollout APIs, telemetry. No model payloads should traverse control-plane endpoints.
- Data-plane attachments (inference traffic) should be routed locally; for on-prem we recommend a direct L3 adjacency (BGP) into the inference pod, with NAT at the edge only for egress to third-party services (not to Redwood control).

3) Network expectations / MTU / BGP:
- Default MTU: 1500; if colo / carrier imposes jumbo frames (9000), we require MTU negotiation on the edge and will adjust path MTU on the pod fabric.
- BGP: we support single-hop EBGP from customer edge; ask for ASN, prefix advertisement plan, and community tags. We'll accept /29 control-plane peering when required.

4) Audit & logging:
- API audit logs: retained in customer-owned S3 (recommended) or pushed to customer SIEM via TLS syslog. We provide signed manifests for rollbacks and a parity log for 90 days by default.
- Access logs: token-level traces are available in Console; for Private deployments we can forward token-level events to an S3 bucket with object-level encryption.

5) KMS/HSM options:
- Option A: Redwood-managed HSM with customer-supplied wrapping keys (fastest).
- Option B: Customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) via cross-account grants — requires IAM policy and a short rotation window (90 days default).

Next steps / deliverables:
- I'll update pvpc-controlplane-diagram-v2 with: CIDR blocks, egress IP set, and BGP ASN placeholders.
- Kim: provide the E2E cutover checklist and a minimal evidence pack for Acme security (SOC-like items).
- Marissa: confirm timeline for the hands-on workshop; I suggest Mon Aug 26 for the lab run.

Drive link for draft diagram: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fPVPC-controls-exchange

--
